💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pokemon fans have been left disappointed after a cryptic countdown from The Pokemon Company turned out to be a 30th-anniversary music video rather than fresh information about Gen 10.
  • Since October, Pokemon’s Japanese X account had been posting anniversary images featuring different Pokemon and the franchise’s 30th anniversary logo.
  • The posts offered no explanation for what would happen when the timer reached zero.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pokemon fans have been left disappointed after a cryptic countdown from The Pokemon Company turned out to be a 30th-anniversary music video rather than fresh information about Gen 10.

Since October, Pokemon’s Japanese X account had been posting anniversary images featuring different Pokemon and the franchise’s 30th anniversary logo. The National Pokedex number for the Pokemon featured in each image appeared to represent the hours remaining until November 30, with the countdown eventually pointing to a reveal at 2 p.m. UTC.

The posts offered no explanation for what would happen when the timer reached zero. That led fans to speculate that Pokemon could finally reveal more about Gen 10, including another look at Winds and Waves, a upcoming Pokemon Presents, or long-requested announcements such as Ruby and Sapphire ports.

Confirmation. We have a third data point676 hours from now is 14:00 UTC on November 30th 2026.As I predicted, they are counting down to then. What will arrive at that point, it remains a mystery but I am excited pic.twitter.com/68gFMSOy9M.

The Pokemon Company revealed that the countdown was leading to Pokemon Special Music Video “Evergreen,” a new animated project celebrating the franchise’s 30th anniversary.

According to recent reports, the video will feature a song by Official HIGE DANdism, with animation produced by MADHOUSE and direction from Naoko Yamada. It will premiere on the official Pokemon YouTube channel on November 30 at 11 p.m. JST, or 2 p.m. UTC. The “Evergreen” song will then be released digitally on December 1.

A newly introduced Pokémon special music video, “Evergreen,” premieres November 30 at 6 a.m. PST! 🎉Song: “Evergreen” by OFFICIAL HIGE DANDISMAnimation: MADHOUSEDirector: Naoko YamadaFollow the link and hit “Notify me” 🛎️ https://t.co/uxEsCIkXmb#Pokemon30 #OnwardWithPokemon pic.twitter.com/vjXpj8qRmf.

Pokemon described the project as the conclusion to its year-long “Pokemon to Tsuzuku,” or “Continuing with Pokemon,” anniversary campaign. The announcement was met with mixed reactions from fans who had spent weeks trying to work out what the countdown meant.

CentroLeaks mentioned the video would mark the finale of Pokemon’s 30th anniversary, while one fan posted, “I got excited for nothing.” Another questioned the point of counting down to “a f***ing music video no one on the planet cares about.”.

Pokemon calls 2026 its “best year yet” for 30th anniversary as Gen 10 speculation grows.

Pokemon responds after official X account hacked to sell memecoin.

Pokemon Center UK delays 30th Celebration ETB orders by two months on release day.

According to The Pokémon Tech giant this video will mark the finale of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary.

Other fans were more open to the idea, especially because the project could resemble 2020’s popular “GOTCHA!” music video, which was set to Bump of Chicken’s “Acacia.” One fan argued that if “Evergreen” reaches the same standard, it could still be “some good s***” for the anniversary’s animation lineup.

Industry observers note that however, the reveal still frustrated fans hoping for Gen 10 news. “We could’ve gotten Winds/Waves but nope,” one post read, calling the countdown “lame and pathetic” and saying it was not worth the buildup.

The music video may be the finale for Pokemon’s 30th Anniversary celebration, so fans expecting a Gen 10 announcement may have to wait for Pokemon Day in February 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Think of it as many nodes connected to each other via edges.
  • A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

The pages of a site form a graph. Think of it as many nodes connected to each other via edges. Each of the edges are the links between the pages, and the nodes themselves are the pages. Now if you start to visualize this as a graph, you will promptly see that there are multiple ways to traverse this graph and reach a particular endpoint.

A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).

Industry observers note that if a page lies very deep from the home page, it means that it's not an key page. It's an indication to the search engine that this is not something that you yourself consider important, and the search engine has a lesser incentive to rank this page over pages that are linked better within your site.

Sources indicate that the key metric here is link depth. That is the number of clicks it takes to reach a particular page from your home page.

Another key metric is broken links. If you have too many broken links, it indicates to the search engine that your site is outdated and not well maintained, and the search engine will then not want to rank your site.

The way to identify both these problems is the same: to actually walk through your site, do a crawl of your site outside in, and try to figure out what the link depth is and if there are broken links on your website.

Recent findings suggest that seed the crawl with the home page and all URLs mentioned in the sitemap. Technically, the sitemap is not required if you're doing a crawl, but going from the sitemap will allow us to detect orphaned pages as well.

It has been revealed that fetch the pages and follow redirects as required. Record when you're following a redirect: we do not let fetch follow it silently, we record each hop and add its target to the crawl. Record HTTP errors as they occur.

Drop URL fragments and tracking parameters. Keep trailing slashes because sometimes there can be mismatches around expectation of trailing slashes in different URLs of a site.

Industry observers note that in order to navigate from the home page, we can use BFS. So we know that the first time we reach a page, that is the page's shortest path.

We can cut off the depth over a certain threshold, say 5, to indicate that pages beyond that are too far or too deep to be reached.

Noindex pages will still be crawled. However, we need to make a record of them being not indexed, to reflect that they will not be present in the search engine.

The desired page depth is as close to the home page as possible. Important pages should be close to the home page. The deeper you go from the home page, it signals to the search engine that the page is less important.

A couple of examples of how a deep page is present:.

The suggested fix for this is that we link the pages from as close to the home page as possible:.

Wasted links are those internal links that do not do the job they're supposed to do. The different types of wasted links:.

In a recent development, we have seen here how to look at our own website through the lens of a search engine. You can use some of the code over here to create your own crawler and identify internal linking issues; the full script is in this gist. Alternatively, we can use a free internal link visualizer to identify these issues and focus only on the fixes to improve our site's internal linking.

  • Now, McDonald’s is experimenting with a different preparation method that would see employees bread chicken by hand inside its restaurants, alongside the introduction of a upcoming spicy chicken sandwich.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

McDonald’s has begun testing hand-battered chicken in select US markets as the fast food giant explores a potential nationwide rollout of the menu items.

The company has continued to expand its chicken offerings in recent years, with the McCrispy sandwich and McCrispy Strips becoming part of its permanent menu.

Now, McDonald’s is experimenting with a different preparation method that would see employees bread chicken by hand inside its restaurants, alongside the introduction of a upcoming spicy chicken sandwich.

Recent findings suggest that on November 23, McDonald’s franchisee account McFranchisee revealed that the chain is testing its hand-breaded chicken menu in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and the Tucson, Arizona, area. A similar test is also taking place in Ireland.

All five items are also available as meals, with prices ranging from $8.19 to $9.99 at the location shown.

It has been revealed that 🚨 The two test markets for @McDonalds hand-battered chicken have been revealed: Baton Rouge & Tucson area (Ireland also testing concurrently).The test assesses customer demand, kitchen complexity, and overall economics. Some franchisees have concerns over increased labor… https://t.co/FRupoGRnen pic.twitter.com/0xpHygRNn4.

According to McFranchisee, the McSpicy marks the first time McDonald’s has offered a spicy breaded chicken sandwich of its kind in the US since a short-lived rollout in 2006. The sandwich differs from the version sold in Asian markets, which uses thigh meat.

The test is designed to assess customer demand, kitchen complexity, and the financial viability of introducing hand-breaded chicken across the country.

Some franchisees have reportedly raised concerns about the additional labor hours, kitchen operations, and potential remodeling costs associated with the preparation method.

McFranchisee previously shared footage in June showing employees preparing hand-breaded Spicy McWings, alongside comments attributed to McDonald’s CEO about introducing hand-breaded chicken in the US.

A fresh Steam game that lets players explore the internet and play minigames together in a single web browser could become your group’s next obsession.

From viral browser games that allow you to stroke virtual cats to gacha games that let players battle it out in Pokemon card-style battles with Wikipedia pages, 2026 has been a fantastic year for weird and wonderful games.

Joining this list is INTERNET4, an upcoming Steam game that lets you and your friends fish, compete in general knowledge quizzes, draw, and browse the internet together.

Recent findings suggest that browsing the significant World Wide Web is usually a solitary thing, but the developers behind INTERNET4 have decided this no longer needs to be the case. Instead, you and eight buddies will be able to team up and explore websites together.

The main highlight is Wikipedia Challenge, which creates minigames based on information from the popular website and those across the web. You’ll need to follow information between articles to reach the target page, while Research Battle has you investigating a random topic.

According to recent reports, the latter requires you to show off your answer and even vote amongst your pals to choose the winner. There’s also a more relaxed fishing minigame (who doesn’t like a bit of video game fishing?) where you can catch, record, and compare your bites while surfing the net.

According to recent reports, tuning into your favorite livestreams and watching videos together is also an option for those who would rather spend their time doomscrolling memes. INTERNET4 also lets you plan trips by exploring destinations or pull up a game map to discuss strategies between adrenaline-filled gaming sessions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Latest Jersey pizzeria has been bombarded with death threats, fake orders and one-star reviews after an online mob confused it with another restaurant at the center of a viral feud.
  • Electronics repair shop owner Leone Mastrolia, better known on social media as Digital Doctor, found himself embroiled in a dispute with the owner of Nick’s Pizza, located in the same shopping complex as his business in Manahawkin.
  • According to recent reports, the drama began when a customer offered to buy Mastrolia lunch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Latest Jersey pizzeria has been bombarded with death threats, fake orders and one-star reviews after an online mob confused it with another restaurant at the center of a viral feud.

Electronics repair shop owner Leone Mastrolia, better known on social media as Digital Doctor, found himself embroiled in a dispute with the owner of Nick’s Pizza, located in the same shopping complex as his business in Manahawkin.

According to recent reports, the drama began when a customer offered to buy Mastrolia lunch. The content creator declined pizza from the neighboring restaurant, citing ongoing issues with his landlord.

The pizzeria’s owner subsequently contacted police, accusing Mastrolia of harassment after the restaurant began receiving negative reviews.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

Mastrolia filmed his interaction with police and uploaded it to social media, with the viral video amassing over 3.1 million views in less than a day.

However, some viewers looking to retaliate against the restaurant ended up targeting an entirely unrelated business.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

Nick’s Pizza and Pasta in Cinnaminson, located more than an hour away from the restaurant involved in the dispute, received upwards of 60 one-star reviews in a single day.

According to New Jersey 101.5, trolls accused the restaurant of serving expired food and having infestations of mice and cockroaches.

According to recent reports, things escalated when employees began receiving threatening phone calls. Restaurant owner Nick Lubrano and his wife, Sonia Scotto, said one caller even threatened to murder their family.

“I’m gonna kill your family,” the caller reportedly said.

The restaurant was also inundated with suspicious orders, including one from a California phone number requesting eight large pepperoni pizzas.

Restaurant hits out at “miserable and entitled” diners after viral outrage over tips rule.

Pizza restaurant faces backlash after confronting 5-year-old’s birthday party for bringing cake.

Internet rallies behind Red Baron worker who snapped at Instagram prankster.

The couple eventually learned what had happened after someone spotted the viral videos and contacted them about the mix-up.

Sources indicate that fortunately, Mastrolia took it upon himself to make things right. In a follow-up video, the repair shop owner visited the pizzeria, apologized in person and handed over $1,000, suggesting the money be used to give away free pizzas or reward employees.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

He also urged his followers to stop leaving negative reviews for businesses they had never visited, regardless of whether they had found the right restaurant.

“Thanks Leo for driving up and personally apologizing to us on behalf of your followers,” Nick’s replied. “Shows your integrity and we respect that a lot!”.

Meanwhile, longtime customers rallied behind the family-owned pizzeria, which has been operating in Cinnaminson for 14 years, leaving positive reviews and messages of support to counter the online backlash.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fortnite might have signed up four new club members, and a leaker spilled their names before Epic could even unlock the door.

The roster was already crowded, since Treasure Hunters had spent November piling anime crossovers onto Crossbones Isle, from the One Piece crew to Hatsune Miku. This next arrival, however, hails from a game that spends its opening act masquerading as a cutesy dating sim before it starts shredding players’ nerves, which makes it a strange fit for a battle royale that’s apparently making room for it anyway.

Recent findings suggest that on November 24, HYPEX claimed that Doki Doki Literature Club would land in Fortnite within the week, bringing the club’s four leading ladies along: Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri, and Monika. According to the leaker, no other cosmetics will tag along, so don’t hold out for a poem-shaped pickaxe.

DOKI DOKI LITERATURE CLUB IS COMING TO FORTNITE WITHIN 1 WEEKSayori, Natsuki, Yuri & Monika, no other cosmetics pic.twitter.com/KgA74cuct6.

In a recent development, the post built on what HYPEX first dredged up on November 12, when an encrypted set of four female cel-shaded skins surfaced in the game’s files. Each came with a custom lobby pose, at least two sported cloth physics, and one flaunted special hair physics. At the time, the leaker also said the skins would sell as a bundle as well as individually.

Epic Games hasn’t announced the collab yet, and prices remain under wraps. Still, with Treasure Hunters barreling toward its December 5 finale, the club doesn’t have long to make its entrance.

The choice of franchise raised a few eyebrows, too. Team Salvato’s 2017 visual novel lured players in with cheery classmates and a poetry club before swerving hard into psychological horror, and its Steam page still warns that it isn’t suitable for children.

Fortnite itself remains rated T for Teen, although its ESRB listing picked up a Suggestive Themes descriptor back in August after a wave of more revealing skins caught players’ attention.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pastor Tyler Sterban of Different Church in Nashville brought a TV and PlayStation 5 onto the stage and played GTA 6 during a Sunday sermon, using the long-awaited release as a controversial object lesson.
  • Sterban co-pastors Different Church with his wife, Ry’Ann.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 launched on November 19 after more than a decade of anticipation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pastor Tyler Sterban of Different Church in Nashville brought a TV and PlayStation 5 onto the stage and played GTA 6 during a Sunday sermon, using the long-awaited release as a controversial object lesson.

Sterban co-pastors Different Church with his wife, Ry’Ann. The church’s website claims the pair came from non-churched backgrounds and have spent nine years in ministry. Sterban has also used unusual demonstrations in previous services, including taking off his pants during a January sermon about staying spontaneous and ready.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 launched on November 19 after more than a decade of anticipation. Its Mature 17+ rating and depictions of violence, nudity, strong sexual content, drugs and alcohol have also made it a target for Christian and conservative critics.

Industry observers note that "Let me go punch somebody… How do I punch? Oh wait I gotta go to somebody, don't I?"Pastor Tyler Sterban of 'Different Church' plays GTA6 (Grand Theft Auto VI) during their Sunday morning service for a sermon illustration. pic.twitter.com/ltomUYbQl8.

Clips of the sermon show Sterban playing GTA 6 while speaking to the congregation about the 13-year wait for Rockstar’s sequel.

He recalled fans repeatedly joking that they had “got this before GTA 6” and compared the anticipation surrounding the game with the patience Christians are expected to show in their faith.

“Isn’t it crazy how we can wait for GTA better than we can wait for God?” Sterban said during the sermon.

It has been revealed that as he moved through the game, Sterban tried to work out how to attack an in-game character, creating the most unexpected moment in the clip. Protestia also reported that a staff member or friend paid $100 for the game as a sacrifice for the ministry.

Sterban claimed that GTA 6 is not appropriate for people to play, framing the demonstration as an object lesson rather than an endorsement of the game’s content.

The pastor’s decision comes as GTA 6 faces an unusual amount of scrutiny from religious communities. Pastor Landon Chase argued that no Christian man can play the game without sinning, while Pastor Carlos Erazo said Christians should skip it because progressing through the story requires players to engage with content that conflicts with their beliefs.

Conservative commentators have criticized GTA 6 for different reasons. Fox News contributors called out fans who took time off work to play it and raised concerns about the game’s violence, while several online influencers complained that the story asks players to treat Lucia with respect.

Against that backdrop, Sterban’s sermon has drawn attention because it puts the game inside the church while acknowledging the same concerns critics have raised about it.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Running an AI agent on your own GPU sounds simple: point it at Ollama and stop paying per token. I set up OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, with a 9B model in Ollama on one RTX 3090 and connected it to Discord. Then I read the Ollama log for every request.

It has been revealed that the agent worked. The numbers were not what I expected, though. A one-line question turned into a prompt of more than 18,000 tokens, the first reply took over a minute, and the small model sometimes guessed instead of using its tools.

This article covers what I measured and what each number means if you proposal to run an agent on local hardware.

OpenClaw ran in Docker and reached Ollama on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434. Discord was the chat interface, and OpenClaw's web panel revealed the sessions and context use.

In a recent development, this article is about the results, not the installation. The full step-by-step setup is in a separate guide to running OpenClaw in Docker with Ollama and Discord. That guide covers the Compose file, the Discord bot and how to keep the ports off your network.

In a recent development, all timings below come from the Ollama log on the test machine. Ollama loaded the model with a 32,768-token context.

My first message in Discord was short: "Which model are you running on, and what is 17 * 23?" The bot answered correctly: it ran on ollama/qwen3.5:9b, and 17 × 23 is 391.

Recent findings suggest that the Ollama log demonstrated what that question cost. The model processed 18,415 prompt tokens and generated 33 tokens.

According to recent reports, the extra tokens come from the agent itself. With every request, OpenClaw sends:.

Recent findings suggest that on the RTX 3090, reading that prompt took 10 seconds at 1,838 tokens per second. A slower GPU, or a CPU, needs much longer to read the same prompt.

Sources indicate that prompt tokens per model call, from the Ollama log. Only the first message had to process the whole prompt.

OpenClaw counts tokens with its own estimate, which was higher than the Ollama count. The gateway log estimated the prompt at 24,608 tokens, against a prompt budget of 24,576 tokens for this model. By OpenClaw's own count, the base prompt alone used up the budget before any conversation history.

The web panel showed a similar figure: 68 to 69 percent of the context window was in use for the Discord sessions after only a few messages.

The first message arrived while the model was not loaded in GPU memory. That reply took 1 min 10 s:.

The next requests were much faster:.

Reply times on the test machine. Loading the model took most of the first reply.

Recent findings suggest that the speed-up comes from prompt caching. The system prompt, tool definitions and workspace files at the start of the prompt stay the same between requests. Ollama kept that part cached and processed only the new tokens. The model wrote at 91 to 96 tokens per second in every test.

Ollama's documentation says models stay in memory for 5 minutes by default before they are unloaded. After that, the next message pays the load time again. You can change this with the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable on the Ollama server, or with the keep_alive parameter per request. A negative value, such as -1, keeps the model loaded. I did not change this setting in the test.

If you run Ollama in Docker, pass the variable with -e OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 or in the environment: section of your Compose file.

Two things used the GPU besides my chat messages.

Recent findings suggest that A heartbeat. OpenClaw's web panel listed one scheduled automation, heartbeat-main, which runs every 30 minutes. The agent wakes on that schedule, so the model gets called even when nobody chats. With Ollama's 5-minute default, the model is unloaded between heartbeats unless someone chatted recently, so a heartbeat most likely starts with a model load. I did not measure this.

An embedding model. During the first message, OpenClaw also called Ollama's /api/embed endpoint twice to index its memory. It used qwen3-embedding:4b, which was already installed on the Ollama server. I did not set OpenClaw to use that model; it picked it on its own.

The two models took this much GPU memory:.

That is 11.4 GB for the models alone, almost half of the RTX 3090's 24 GB.

The rest of the stack was light:.

What this means for you: proposal GPU memory for the chat model, the embedding model and the context, not the chat model alone. If the GPU also runs other models, the heartbeat can compete with them.

The first two tests in Discord: a question, then a file written with a tool. The user name is blurred.

The mistakes indicated up when the model had to check something:.

It has been revealed that after the restart, the bot claimed it had lost the earlier session. When asked to use its read tool, it read the file correctly.

According to recent reports, the fix for the first problem was simple. When I wrote "use your read tool to open homelab-test.md", the model opened the file and listed all three points correctly. Naming the tool made it check instead of guess.

The model listed four files and missed the test file and a folder, because it answered from its prompt.

Based on this test, a local 9B model on one consumer GPU works for:.

If you need better answers, OpenClaw also works with hosted models, but then your prompts leave your machine.

According to recent reports, in this test, qwen3.5:9b used 6.3 GB and the qwen3-embedding:4b memory model used 5.1 GB. Together the two models needed 11.4 GB.

It has been revealed that the model had to load into GPU memory first, which took 59 seconds of the 70-second reply. Ollama keeps a model loaded for 5 minutes by default, and the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE setting changes that.

Sources indicate that every request includes OpenClaw's system prompt, its tool definitions and its workspace files. A one-line question became an 18,415-token prompt in this test.

Yes. A heartbeat automation runs every 30 minutes and calls the model even when nobody sends a message.

Sources indicate that it handled questions, arithmetic and file creation correctly in this test. It sometimes answered from its prompt instead of using its tools. When it wrongly stated its memory was lost, asking it to use its read tool made it check the file and answer correctly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, growth at MotorCity Casino outweighed declines at MGM Grand Detroit and Hollywood Casino at Greektown, lifting Detroit's October table and slot revenue from a year earlier. Retail sports betting also rebounded sharply from September, adding to the month's gains.

MotorCity Casino was the only Detroit property to grow table games and slot revenue in October from a year earlier. Its rivals both lost ground. MGM Grand Detroit slipped 2.7% to $51.3 million. Hollywood Casino at Greektown fell 5.0% to $21.6 million.

Across the three casinos, tables and slots generated $108.1 million. That was up 2.1% from October 2025 and 5.2% from September 2026. Year-to-date revenue from January through October was up 2.3%.

CDC Gaming Reports put October 2025 table and slot revenue at $105.9 million.

MGM still holds the largest piece of the market. It took 47% of Detroit’s October revenue. MotorCity held 33%, and Hollywood Casino at Greektown held 20%.

The October split continues a pattern from late summer. In August, MotorCity rose 8.3% to $33.8 million and MGM grew 2.3% to $52.9 million, while Greektown fell 2.6% to $22.2 million, InterGame reported. Detroit’s August total was $109.7 million.

Industry observers note that greektown’s slide deepened in September, when its revenue fell 8.8% year over year to $21.34 million. October’s decline was smaller. MGM, by contrast, moved from growth in August to a decline in October.

Sources indicate that the citywide trend has been uneven. September table and slot revenue was 4.7% higher than a year earlier but 5.6% lower than in August. October’s rebound lifted aggregate revenue above September’s $103.55 million.

Industry observers note that retail sports betting produced $2.4 million in October. That compares with $769,771 in retail QAGR in September. Handle at the Detroit casinos was $12.87 million for the month.

MotorCity also led the sportsbook results. It posted $928,607 in retail receipts. MGM followed at $746,215, with Hollywood Casino at Greektown close behind at $729,350.

The sportsbook activity generated $90,878 in state taxes. The casinos also sent $111,073 in sports wagering taxes to Detroit.

It has been revealed that the city’s take from the casinos goes well beyond sports betting. In October, Detroit collected $13.4 million from the three properties, combining its share of gaming taxes with sums owed under each casino’s agreement with the city.

A grand total of $9,985,482+ in jackpots hit at MotorCity Casino in October! 💰🎰.

Congratulations to all the guests who took home a win! Here’s to an exciting November! pic.twitter.com/bHIJGmc0jM.

— MotorCity Casino (@MotorCityCasino) November 8, 2026.

Industry observers note that fantasy contests remain a small part of the picture. Operators reported $837,938 in adjusted revenues for September 2026 and paid $70,387 in taxes.

It has been revealed that detroit’s land-based results now set a baseline for Michigan’s October online casino and sports betting figures, which come next. In September, the state’s commercial and tribal online operators took in $355.7 million in combined iGaming and online sports betting gross receipts, 5.4% more than in August.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japanese streamer Haigure Tamao has managed to escape GTA 6’s supposedly impossible six-star Wanted level by using an elaborate Easter egg that transports players into the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.
  • After ditching the sixth Wanted star in GTA 5, Rockstar brought it back for GTA 6, but with a major twist.
  • While players can normally escape the police by changing their appearance, switching vehicles or hiding, reaching six stars is supposed to leave them with just two options: death or arrest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japanese streamer Haigure Tamao has managed to escape GTA 6’s supposedly impossible six-star Wanted level by using an elaborate Easter egg that transports players into the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

After ditching the sixth Wanted star in GTA 5, Rockstar brought it back for GTA 6, but with a major twist.

While players can normally escape the police by changing their appearance, switching vehicles or hiding, reaching six stars is supposed to leave them with just two options: death or arrest.

Even trying to escape in a jet just results in missiles being debuted at you.

GTA VI çıktığı günden beri 6 Yıldız aranma seviyesinden kurtulan kimse olmadı.Eğer jete binersenizFüze atan 5 jet sizi kovalarEğer arabayla kaçarsanız5 taaruz Helikopteri sizi kovalarEğer bir eve saklanırsanız,ordu eve tankla gelir…☠️ pic.twitter.com/5ICWx6QuRv.

However, one player has discovered a clever way to cheat the system with some help from Rockstar’s 2002 classic.

In a video uploaded to YouTube, Tamao, using his VTuber avatar, explained that he wanted to test whether entering the portal featured in GTA 6’s Tommy Vercetti Easter egg would erase his Wanted level.

The secret requires players to solve a puzzle spanning 12 electrical substations across Leonida before accessing a portal inside the Turtle Head Power Station between 7 PM and 6 AM in-game.

Entering it transports Jason to a recreation of the original Malibu Club, complete with PS2-era graphics and an appearance from returning character Kent Paul.

世界初？GTA6で手配度6から逃げきることに成功しました pic.twitter.com/0g7pSPJ6UU.

After struggling to survive his initial attempt, the streamer completed an entirely different secret involving the president’s hidden bunkers to get his hands on a powerful tank.

With his newly acquired vehicle, the YouTuber wreaked havoc near the power station, eventually reaching six stars with just minutes to spare before the portal closed.

It has been revealed that upon entering the retro Vice City, his Wanted level immediately disappeared. However, the biggest question was whether it would return once he was transported back to modern-day Leonida.

“The moment of truth,” Tamao said, translated from Japanese.

Much to his delight, the six stars were nowhere to be seen.

“I finally did it! I went from a Wanted level of six to zero!” he celebrated.

Whether Rockstar intended for players to use the Easter egg this way remains unclear, but the discovery adds yet another layer to one of GTA 6’s most elaborate secrets.

Players have already uncovered some incredible surprises since launch, including Dexter Morgan’s apartment and boat and a glitch that enables first-person gameplay.

As it turns out, the best way to escape Vice City’s police might be to leave their generation of GTA altogether.

Influencer Christie Miller has unveiled her own death at the age of 60 in a pre-recorded video following a four-year battle with breast cancer.

Miller was diagnosed with stage 4 HER2-positive breast cancer in June 2022 and amassed over 50,000 followers on Instagram by documenting her experiences with the disease and encouraging others to find joy in their lives.

The influencer also suffered a devastating personal loss in June 2025 when her husband of 36 years, Mark Miller, died from pancreatic cancer.

On November 23, a video was uploaded to Miller’s Instagram account in which she revealed that she had died and expressed her happiness at being reunited with her late husband.

“If you are seeing this video, it means that I am dead,” she said, before a montage of photos of the couple played alongside Peaches & Herb’s song ‘Reunited.’.

A post shared by Christie Miller | Chief Joy Officer (@iamchristiemiller).

Despite the circumstances surrounding the video, Miller was smiling and dressed in a colorful costume as she reflected on her life.

“Don’t be sad because it’s over, be happy because it happened,” she mentioned, quoting Dr. Seuss.

She encouraged her followers to allow themselves to grieve while also cherishing the memories they had made together.

“I have lived this beautiful life with no regrets,” she remarked.

In the days leading up to her death, Miller continued to share videos of herself enjoying some of her favorite activities.

Miller visited the beach with her dog on November 15 and spent what she believed would be her final week enjoying some of her favorite childhood foods, including a root beer float.

A post shared by Christie Miller | Chief Joy Officer (@iamchristiemiller).

Miller ended her farewell video by encouraging viewers not to let fear or other people’s opinions dictate how they live.

“Go out there and find joy every single day,” she remarked.

The caption accompanying the video confirmed that Miller died peacefully on the morning of November 23, surrounded by love.

Miller is one of several influencers to have recorded their own death announcements. In August 2026, TikToker Andreethegirl shared a final message with her followers after dying from cancer at 39.

Similarly, TikTok stars Tanner Martin and Bella Bradford unveiled their own deaths through pre-recorded videos following their respective battles with cancer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has filed a patent application for a personalized television channel that uses artificial intelligence to generate demonstrates starring the person watching.

Streaming platforms such as YouTube and Netflix already use viewing habits to recommend content, while companies have also started experimenting with broadcasting entirely AI-generated entertainment.

Google’s patent application, titled “Creating a Channel of Video Experiences Tailored to a User,” was originally filed on May 13, 2025, before being published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on November 19, 2026.

First spotted by Patentlyze, the application describes a feature called “My Channel” that would appear within a television app and offer a selection of videos created specifically for individual viewers.

The system would use information including a person’s viewing history, location, language settings, and demographic data to determine what kinds of highlights they might enjoy.

Google could then use photographs to create a digital avatar of the viewer and replicate their voice, allowing them to star in everything from romantic comedies to science fiction adventures.

One example included in the filing describes how the system could generate a video starring someone who had recently watched cricket highlights. The viewer could appear in the stands during the Cricket World Cup or interact with one of their favorite players.

Sources indicate that consumers wouldn’t necessarily have to request latest content, either. The application outlines a scheduling system that could automatically generate videos on a weekly, monthly, or yearly basis. It also describes a mechanism for inserting advertisements into the generated content.

Google now lets anyone make & use their own Android apps using AI.

Latest Microsoft patent could use AI to alter speech and lip movements in real time.

YouTube tests prompt-based custom feeds that let you control your homepage.

However, Google has not announced plans to launch the feature. According to Patentlyze, a patent examiner has issued a final rejection of the application, although the manufacturer can still amend its claims or appeal the decision.

The filing comes as AI-generated programming has already made its way onto streaming platforms, with Roku introducing a television channel dedicated to broadcasting AI-generated content around the clock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games has partnered with Panini to release real-life GTA 6 trading cards based on the collectibles players can find scattered throughout Leonida.

There’s no shortage of things to collect in Grand Theft Auto 6, with Rockstar taking a page out of Red Dead Redemption 2’s book by including hundreds of trading cards for players to hunt down.

There are 480 cards across 18 different sets, ranging from fictional sports stars to comic book characters and nightclub dancers, with players able to sell their rare finds at pawn shops for some extra cash.

Now, just days after GTA 6’s record-breaking launch, Rockstar is giving collectors a chance to rip open packs in real life.

Grand Theft Auto VI official trading cards, coming soon from @PaniniAmerica and @RockstarGames. pic.twitter.com/H1VrYVXTm5.

On November 24, Panini revealed its partnership with Rockstar Games to produce the first officially licensed Grand Theft Auto trading card collection, set to launch in December 2026.

Dubbed the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, the set will recreate cards featuring fictional athletes and teams from Rockstar’s universe.

According to Panini’s product listing, each hobby box will contain four packs of four cards, with collectors pulling an average of two Rookies, one Retro, one Illustrated, and four Special Silvers per box.

Much like real-world sports cards, there will also be rare color variants and numbered parallels, including Bronze Legend cards limited to 49 copies, Silver Legends limited to 25, and coveted one-of-one Gold cards.

It has been revealed that you just know all the down bad GTA 6 players who have fallen head over heels for goth stripper Vicki, will be clamoring for her card. However, the collection may be limited to sports cards for now.

The collaboration is the latest example of Rockstar bringing its fictional world to life, having already created a real-life Grotti Cheetah worth £1 million and teamed up with the Miami Heat for Vice City merchandise.

Panini has yet to announce pricing, an exact release date, or international availability, but considering how much money GTA 6 merchandise has already fetched on the resale market, those one-of-one cards could end up being worth a pretty penny.

The coffee chain introduced its Donutcracker character as part of its 2026 holiday packaging, featuring the festive design on cups, donut boxes, and Munchkins boxes.

Now, starting on Black Friday, November 27, Dunkin’ is bringing the character to life for the first time alongside a series of holiday promotions.

Dunkin’ is installing a 15-foot-tall Donutcracker statue at Historic Fort Steuben’s Christmas at the Fort celebration in Steubenville, Ohio.

The city is home to the world’s largest collection of life-size nutcrackers, with the Dunkin’ character set to join more than 200 others at the holiday attraction.

Visitors can also purchase exclusive Donutcracker merchandise at the Dunkin’ restaurant at 1987 Sunset Boulevard in Steubenville while supplies last.

A separate limited-edition merchandise collection will launch on November 27 at noon ET, featuring three items:.

Additional holiday collectibles, including tumblers, ornaments, and mugs, will arrive at participating restaurants nationwide in early December, with prices ranging from $12.99 to $34.99.

Alongside the Donutcracker’s debut, Dunkin’ is bringing back its Free Donut Fridays promotion for three consecutive weeks.

Dunkin’ Rewards members can claim a free Classic Donut with any qualifying beverage purchase on November 27, December 4, and December 11 at participating US locations.

Customers can redeem the offer by ordering through the Dunkin’ app, scanning their Rewards ID at checkout, or paying with an enrolled Dunkin’ card.

The promotion is limited to one free donut per member each Friday and excludes specialty donuts. Both the beverage and donut must be included in the same order, and the offer cannot be combined with other promotions or Meal Deals.

Latest Update: Best Ecommerce Platforms for Developers: Six Options and the Layers Each Leaves You

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (730 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • According to recent reports, 7 Day Free Trial.
  • Picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

According to recent reports, 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath. Every platform below draws that line in a different place. If you have already settled the front-end question with a comparison like SitePoint's Astro vs Next.js guide, the next question is what sits behind it. Prices are from each vendor's pricing page as of November 2026.

Shopify is the fully managed option. Basic costs $29 a month with card rates from 2.9% plus 30 cents, and a 2% fee applies to orders processed through a third-party gateway on that plan. Developers get two routes: Liquid themes, or Hydrogen, Shopify's headless toolkit, where your framework owns routing and rendering and Hydrogen supplies the Storefront API client and cart. Templates exist for React Router on Oxygen and for Next.js on Vercel. Plus starts at $2,300 a month.

Whop is a business platform for taking payments and sending payouts, and it sits under a storefront you have already built rather than replacing it. The Checkout element runs in the browser with no server code and no API key on the page. You pass your own order ID as metadata, Whop copies it onto the payment, and your server fulfills from a signed webhook that follows the Standard Webhooks spec. Domestic cards cost 2.7% plus 30 cents with no monthly fee, buyers see payment methods chosen by their location across 195 countries, and the same balance pays out in over 200 countries, including to affiliates or sellers you onboard. Whop's own guide shows how to integrate a checkout API into a Next.js storefront end to end. The trade-off is that there is no catalog or shipping engine; you collect address fields at checkout and trigger fulfillment from the webhook.

It has been revealed that wooCommerce is a free plugin on WordPress you host yourself, so you own updates, security, and performance. Its payment gateway, WooPayments, charges US merchants 2.9% plus 30 cents per card transaction, 1.5% more for international cards, 2% for currency conversion, and $25 per dispute. Everything is PHP hooks and filters, which makes it the natural pick for agencies already living in WordPress and the wrong pick for anyone who does not want to run a server.

BigCommerce hosts the back end and lets you bring any front end. Core is $29 a month billed annually, capped at $30,000 in trailing annual sales, and prepares auto-upgrade as volume grows. There are no platform fees when you use an embedded payment provider, and a 2% fee on Core if you use another one. Catalyst, its reference storefront, is built on Next.js, React Server Components, and the Storefront GraphQL API, and deploys to Vercel.

Medusa is an open-source commerce framework in Node.js and TypeScript, with an MIT-licensed core and a commercial enterprise edition. SitePoint covered it when it was still a young Shopify alternative; it now has over 37,000 GitHub stars. Self-hosting is free. Medusa Cloud starts at $29 a month for development, $99 for launch, and $299 for scale, with no percentage of sales, and the company claims you can export your data and self-host at any point.

Saleor is a GraphQL-native, API-only commerce platform written in Python and released under the BSD-3 license. Self-hosting is free. Saleor Cloud starts at $1,599 a month for up to $200,000 in monthly sales, with 0.8% on orders above that, and $3,999 a month at the next tier. It is built for teams with a dedicated engineering function and a large catalog, which is exactly who should pay that price.

As reported by Delish, Costco’s Kirkland Signature Turkey Dinner Kit has returned to the retailer’s deli department for 2026.

Each kit comes with a seasoned, boneless half turkey breast, herbed stuffing, Yukon Gold mashed potatoes, green beans, cranberry sauce, and gravy.

The kits are priced at $3.99 per pound and weigh around 10 pounds, meaning shoppers can expect to pay roughly $40 for the entire meal.

According to Costco’s official product listing, each kit serves seven to eight people, bringing the cost down to around $5 per person.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that west Virginia's online casinos posted record monthly revenue in October 2026, the second full month with bet365 live in the state. The result pushed 2026 revenue past the total for all of 2025, while a bill to raise the iGaming tax remains pending.

Industry observers note that the revenue measure is adjusted gross interactive wagering receipts. State law defines it as an operator’s gross online wagering receipts minus winnings paid to players. Under 2019’s House Bill 2934, the privilege tax on those receipts goes into the Interactive Wagering Fund each week, and every licensed racetrack and historic resort pays it.

bet365 launched online sports betting and casino in the state on Aug. 27, 2026. West Virginia is its fourth U.S. online casino state. In its other 14 states, bet365 offers sports betting only.

Recent findings suggest that lottery licensing documents show bet365 received an interim license in January 2026. It was approved for a full annual license on July 29. West Virginia was the organization’s sixth North American launch in 13 months, Yogonet reported. The earlier rolls out were Kansas and Maryland in August 2025, Missouri in December 2025, Michigan in April 2026 and Alberta in July 2026.

West Virginia’s market has a fixed structure. The Interactive Wagering Act allows no more than five gaming facility licenses with online wagering. Every online game counts as a state-owned lottery game. October’s record is consistent with bet365 adding to that market, but the operator split has yet to be shown.

Industry observers note that two months of 2026 remain to be reported. The comparison months set a high bar. Adjusted gross interactive gaming receipts were $37,198,210 in November 2025. Receipts for the fiscal year to date through Nov. 30, 2025, were $169,425,990.

Industry observers note that the broader lottery picture also reveals growth. The Lottery took in more than $1.33 billion in gross revenue in fiscal 2026, which ended June 30. It sent $582.9 million to the state. Revenue was $58 million higher than in fiscal 2025. In its fiscal 2026 wrap-up, the Lottery named iLottery and iGaming as its biggest growth areas, and said iGaming was following national gaming trends.

Higher revenue also raises the stakes of a pending tax change. Introduced on Jan. 16, 2026, House Bill 4397 would increase the iGaming privilege tax. The bill is still listed as pending in the House Local Governments Committee.

According to recent reports, the next detail to watch is the operator breakdown. The Lottery publishes a file that splits interactive wagering data by skin and casino. That file will show how much of October’s record came from bet365.

“Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan mentioned.

Logan Coomes, whose garage was struck, mentioned an Amazon Prime Air team arrived within 10 minutes of the crash and worked with local utility workers to remove the drone by early evening.

The firm reportedly offered to help repair the damaged roof and gave Coomes a $100 Amazon gift card.

In a statement shared with CNN, an Amazon spokesperson said its Prime Air drones conduct nearly 6,000 flights per day and have delivered “hundreds of thousands of packages this year.”.

Amazon also mentioned the incident marked the first crash of its kind involving its drone delivery operations near Detroit.

Earlier in November, 17-year-old Kylie Arellano was rescued after secretly asking another player for help while playing Innersloth’s popular social deduction game.

Sources indicate that arellano had been missing since May 2025, when she disappeared from her home in Utah at the age of 15. She was allegedly held against her will in the basement of a home in Huntington, Oregon.

For Colorado teenager Landon Tresp, what began as an ordinary gaming session on October 15 would end with him helping a girl hundreds of miles away escape her alleged captor.

After meeting in Among Us, Landon and Arellano struck up a friendship and began communicating through Discord.

“We just kind of clicked,” Landon stated.

Over the following two weeks, Arellano began opening up about her situation, eventually sending Landon news articles covering her disappearance.

Realizing something was seriously wrong, Landon turned to his mother, Khristina, for help on Halloween. Neither knew that within 24 hours, the girl would finally be free.

Khristina began speaking with Arellano through Discord, but locating the teenager proved challenging as she didn’t know the address where she was being held.

“I knew I had to do everything I could to make sure she was brought to safety and had a second chance,” Khristina recalled.

Recent findings suggest that determined to find her, Khristina searched online property records before turning to real estate website Zillow. After being sent photos of two potential houses, Arellano recognized the second property.

Khristina contacted the girl’s family and began working with the FBI to bring her home.

Speaking with KOAA, Khristina described how devastating it was to learn just how long Arellano had been missing.

“Just heartbreaking to think that she had been going through what she had for over 520 days and without anyone that she could reach a hand out to and not knowing where you’re at,” she mentioned.

On November 1, authorities arrived at the Oregon residence. Khristina stayed on a video call with Arellano, encouraging her to make the final few steps toward freedom.

“I was on the video chat with her when I told her to face those basement stairs and run up them and down that hallway,” Khristina recalled. “And grab that front door because that was her freedom.”.

After more than 500 days away from home, Arellano was finally in the care of law enforcement and was taken for medical treatment and evaluation.

For Landon, seeing the friend he had met just weeks earlier finally reach safety was an overwhelming moment.

“Oh my God, just pure bliss. I was so happy she was safe in that car. I was so happy she was out of that horrible monster’s house,” he remarked.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, has since been indicted on a federal charge of transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Prosecutors allege he met the girl online before traveling to Utah and taking her across state lines.

Despite everything that happened, Landon and Arellano haven’t stopped playing video games together.

The pair remain friends, while Khristina continues to speak with Arellano every day. The family is also hoping to meet her in person.

What began with two strangers meeting in Among Us has become a friendship that extends far beyond the game, with Landon and his mother giving Arellano the help she had desperately needed for more than a year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games has revealed several features that were scrapped during the development of GTA 6, including activities that were available in previous Grand Theft Auto games.

After years of anticipation, GTA 6 has finally arrived, introducing players to Leonida alongside the franchise’s newest protagonists, Jason and Lucia. The game has also earned a Metacritic score of 99, matching The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

However, despite the number of activities available throughout the open world, Rockstar has revealed that several planned gameplay mechanics and returning features never made it into the finished game.

Speaking to German outlet PC Games, Rockstar North development manager Rob Nelson and design producer Scott Mitchell discussed several features that were considered during development but ultimately abandoned.

Among them was tennis, which players could participate in throughout GTA 5. Rockstar had planned to bring the activity back for GTA 6, but its implementation failed to meet the developer’s standards. Mini golf, however, made it into the finished game.

GTA 6 features that were cut, per a PC Games interview with Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell of Rockstar North:Tennis (planned, but didn't meet Rockstar's standards)Cinema and theatre visits (not interactive enough)CrawlingHome decoratingCraftingSource:… pic.twitter.com/NviyEdt2M9.

It has been revealed that the developers also revealed that players were originally going to be able to crawl, decorate their homes, and craft items. These mechanics were ultimately scrapped, with some not fitting the game’s story or gameplay.

Cinema and theater visits were also removed, as Rockstar felt the activities were not interactive enough.

Nelson also explained how Red Dead Redemption 2 influenced the development of GTA 6, particularly when it came to storytelling and the relationship between its two protagonists.

The Western’s approach to pacing encouraged Rockstar to incorporate quieter moments into GTA 6, giving Jason and Lucia more opportunities for character development between the game’s action sequences.

Industry News: Your SSL certificates can now last 200 days at most: The real risk isn’t renewal

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1194 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • It has been revealed that every SSL certificate comes with a limited lifespan.
  • In a recent development, so what does this mean if you already look after sites with SSL certificates, and will it bring drastic changes?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

It has been revealed that every SSL certificate comes with a limited lifespan. Following the latest upgrade from the CA/Browser Forum, the maximum lifetime of a certificate has fallen from 398 days to 200, and it will drop to 100 days in March 2027 and 47 days in 2029. Renewal is no longer an annual chore. It’s an ongoing task that only stays manageable with automation.

In a recent development, so what does this mean if you already look after sites with SSL certificates, and will it bring drastic changes? For many setups, very little will change. For others, one missed renewal can mean an outage. This article explains what’s changing and what to do if you’re in the second group.

Industry observers note that today, an SSL certificate is valid for 200 days at most. The limit applies when a certificate is issued, so the ones you already hold keep their original expiration date.

In a recent development, where you feel it depends on how your certificates renew. Sites on managed hosting platforms or behind a content delivery network (CDN) usually renew automatically already, often every 90 days, so the upcoming limit changes little. The pressure lands on setups where someone buys a certificate once a year and installs it by hand. At 47 days, that becomes about 12 renewals a year.

Sources indicate that A certificate is a promise from a certificate authority that a key really belongs to a domain, and that promise gets less reliable the longer it runs. If a private key leaks, or a certificate is issued by mistake, it stays usable until it expires. Cutting the lifetime shrinks that window, so a problem that once lingered for over a year is now fixed in weeks.

Shorter lifetimes also make revocation, the process for canceling a bad certificate, far less critical. Revocation has never worked perfectly, but a certificate that expires within weeks matters much less if a cancellation doesn’t reach every browser.

Another reason is about people. A task done once a year is easy to forget and hard to check from outside. Browser makers have pushed for years to move the industry onto automatic renewal, on the logic that a process that runs every few weeks gets tested constantly. If it breaks, you notice swiftly instead of discovering it on the day the certificate expires.

Sources indicate that for most people, the first effect is simply more work. A certificate that once needed attention every year will soon need it every few weeks. Plus, each renewal is a small chance for something to go wrong. Multiply that by dozens of sites, mail servers, and devices, and the chance of one slipping through grows promptly.

The safety nets are also thinner. If you relied on the renewal emails, nothing is watching your certificates now. Additionally, with a shorter life, there’s less time between this should have renewed and this has expired.

According to recent reports, an expired certificate doesn’t make a site slow or dated. It makes it unreachable for most visitors. Chrome, Firefox, and Safari all show a full-page warning that the connection isn’t private, and most people leave instead of clicking through. If the site uses HSTS, a setting that tells browsers to connect only over secure links, there is often no way to click through at all, and visitors are blocked outright until the certificate is fixed.

The damage doesn’t stop at the home page. Checkouts, contact forms, and logins that depend on the secure connection fail along with it, often without an error message that points at the real cause. Other systems break, too, because apps and integrations that call your site over a secure link refuse to connect to an expired certificate.

Industry observers note that nothing about your site has to change for any of this to happen. A date passes, and a site that worked on Friday is down on Monday. In a 47-day lifetime, that date comes around about every six weeks.

Automatic renewal tools do the heavy lifting well. The failures happen around them:.

Look at the five failures above and you’ll see what they share. Each one happens quietly. The renewal job ran, or looked like it did, and nobody checked what the server was actually serving afterwards. Automation can tell you it tried. It can’t tell you the result reached your visitors.

What closes that gap is a check that never relies on your server’s own account of events. Site24x7’s SSL/TLS certificate monitoring does exactly that. It reads the certificate installed on your web server from the cloud, the way a visitor’s browser would, and alerts you before it expires, using thresholds you choose. If a renewal fails quietly, you hear about it from the monitor and not from a customer.

Sources indicate that for each certificate, it records the issuing authority, the owner, the issue date, the expiration date, and the days remaining, including on servers that host several certificates behind one address. That last number matters more as lifespans shrink. When a certificate lasts 47 days, the days left is the figure that tells you a renewal is overdue, and you can set your warning against it using the quarter-of-the-lifetime rule covered next.

Once a monitor is watching your certificates, the next question is when it should speak up.

Most expiration alerts are set to a fixed number of days: warn at 30 days left and escalate at seven. That works for a certificate that lasts a year and renews with a month to spare. It breaks when the whole certificate lasts for a limited number of days.

In a recent development, here’s why: a healthy certificate renews with about a third of its life still left. If your alert appears earlier than that, it goes off on certificates that are doing nothing wrong, and soon everyone ignores it. As lifespans shrink, a fixed 30-day alert will start doing exactly that.

Recent findings suggest that the fix is to set the alerts based on lateness, not on how close the expiry date is. Warn when a quarter of the lifetime is left, since a renewal is overdue by then, and escalate when a tenth is left. Because these are shares of the lifetime, they keep working, however short lifespans get.

The next cut lands on March 15, 2027, so a few checks now will save you from scrambling later:.

Shorter lifespans won’t break your site, but a missed renewal will, so fix the quiet failures now while a mistake still costs an afternoon to fix, not a Monday morning outage affecting lots of customers.

If you’d like a second pair of eyes on your certificates, you can start a 30-day free trial of Site24x7’s SSL/TLS certificate monitoring.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A GTA 6 player has created a website that allows anyone to play Rockstar Games’ latest release for free by remotely taking control of their PS5.

While GTA 6 is currently available on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, those without either console have been left waiting for Rockstar to bring the game to PC.

However, a website called PlayMyPS5 is giving players another way to experience Vice City without having to purchase the game or a console, while attempting to get the internet to complete its story together.

PlayMyPS5 broadcasts gameplay directly from a physical PS5, allowing visitors to join a public queue and remotely control the console through their web browser.

Industry observers note that each player is given five minutes to play before control is handed over to the next person in line. Players have 20 seconds to claim their turn, while remaining idle for 30 seconds will bring their session to an early end.

According to recent reports, the website supports controllers, keyboard and mouse, and mobile touchscreen controls. Players can also watch others explore Vice City and communicate through a live chat while waiting for their turn.

There are no downloads, payments, or registration requirements to join the queue, and players can rejoin once their session ends.

The project was created after its developers realized their PS5 spent much of its time sitting unused. Now, they’re encouraging visitors to work together to complete every GTA 6 story mission.

It has been revealed that the creators are also attempting to raise $993 to purchase a second PS5, allowing more people to play simultaneously and reducing queue times. Other PS5 owners with a copy of GTA 6 can volunteer to share their consoles through the platform.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Uber Eats driver in Massachusetts helped save an elderly woman after hearing her faint cries for help while attempting to complete a delivery.

Brandon McSorley had started delivering orders through Uber Eats to earn extra money ahead of the holiday season when he received an order from a customer in Carver on November 22.

The delivery took him to Cranberry Village, a residential community for people aged 55 and older, where he noticed something was wrong after arriving at the customer’s home.

McSorley told CBS News that the woman had ordered Tylenol and ginger ale. Because the delivery contained medication, he was required to verify the customer’s ID before handing over the order.

However, the house was dark when he arrived, and nobody answered the door. After waiting several minutes and attempting to contact the customer, he began hearing noises from inside the residence.

“I could hear, like, a faint calling. I thought it was potentially someone telling me to go away or something like that,” he said.

In a recent development, mcSorley remained outside until the woman’s cries became clearer, allowing him to hear her asking for help after suffering a fall. He immediately called 911 and waited for emergency services to arrive.

Industry observers note that first responders transported the woman to a nearby hospital. According to Carver EMS, she had been lying on the floor for approximately 45 minutes without access to a phone or a medical alert device.

Carver EMS Chief Michael Ryan credited the delivery driver’s actions with preventing the woman from potentially spending much longer on the floor.

Motorola has posted an updated list of devices getting its Android 17 upgrade, with a few updates already available and many more left to go.

With the update now rolling out to select devices, most recently the Razr Fold, Motorola is confirming an official list of devices getting Android 17.

The list was posted by Motorola Brazil, so this includes devices Motorola doesn’t sell in US markets, and also lists Razr devices without their year naming scheme, rather their international branding – i.e. “Razr (2026)” is “Razr 70.”.

Recent findings suggest that as per usual, Motorola’s update rollouts may see timing vary by region. The Razr Fold update, for example, is currently rolling out in some international markets but has yet to land in the US.

Here’s the full list of Motorola devices officially confirmed to be getting Android 17:.

Industry observers note that among the newly introduced features of Android 17 are improvements to the system interface, with more customization options, new icons, and changes to the layout of buttons and widgets. The Settings menu has been redesigned to make navigation more intuitive and facilitate access to the smartphone’s main functions.

Artificial intelligence in everyday life.

With the update, Circle to Search now offers real-time translations, allowing you to understand content in other languages ​​more easily, without having to interrupt your current activity on your smartphone.

Simplified connectivity and sharing.

Sources indicate that android 17 enhances connectivity with Instant Hotspot , which simplifies sharing your internet connection between compatible devices. Quick Share has also received improvements to facilitate file transfer, including compatibility with iOS smartphones via QR Code.

Industry observers note that security remains a top priority for the system. The Authentication Failure Lock , a security feature in case of theft, locks the screen after unsuccessful authentication attempts. Meanwhile, Message-Based Fraud Detection enhances the identification of potential threats and fraud. Furthermore, access to emergency calls has become easier and faster.

More control over the visual experience.

In a recent development, the revision also improves HDR brightness control, which adjusts the screen intensity to highlight bright details in compatible photos and videos. Users can adjust this brightness for more comfortable viewing, or even disable the feature.

The Motorola Signature 27, the organization’s latest flagship, ships with Android 17 out of the box.

Animal rights organization PETA is urging Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to ditch his iconic black leather jacket, even sending the billionaire an $875 vegan alternative made from olive waste.

Much like Steve Jobs with his black turtlenecks and Mark Zuckerberg with his gray T-shirts, Huang’s leather jackets have become synonymous with the Nvidia boss.

His signature look has even proven lucrative. In July 2026, one of Huang’s signed Tom Ford leather jackets sold for a staggering $960,000 at auction, fetching 16 times its estimated price.

However, following Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO amid an ongoing foreign intelligence investigation for cheating on his wife with an alleged Chinese spy, PETA wants the billionaire to give his wardrobe an upgrade.

In a November 18 letter addressed to Huang, PETA President Tracy Reiman argued that despite his reputation as a technological innovator, his fashion choices were outdated.

Recent findings suggest that “Tech doesn’t move forward by clinging to outdated systems, and neither does fashion,” Reiman said. “PETA is calling on everyone to embrace vegan leathers made from cactus, cork, apples, and other plant materials and leave animals out of their wardrobes.”.

To encourage Huang to make the switch, PETA sent him an $875 jacket from fashion brand Benedetti Life, according to the New York Post.

Sources indicate that the jacket is made using Oleatex, a leather alternative derived from olive harvesting waste. It features an organic cotton lining and an exterior consisting of 95% Biotex and 5% polyurethane.

PETA has also asked Huang to donate his old leather jacket to its planned Museum of Animal-Sourced Atrocities, offering the billionaire the prospect of a tax deduction in return.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid ongoing foreign intelligence investigation.

According to recent reports, interestingly, Huang had already ditched his trademark look when he returned to Nvidia’s headquarters on November 23. However, rather than opting for PETA’s olive-based alternative, he appeared to be sporting a $3,300 Dior cotton jacket, according to GQ.

Whether Huang is willing to part ways with his extensive leather jacket collection remains to be seen. The Nvidia boss previously revealed that he owns between 30 and 40 of them.

The X12 is easily one of the standout options in Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday lineup, and it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a long-term under sink reverse osmosis upgrade and want strong flow, advanced filtration, and plenty of everyday convenience.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An alleged new video shows Galaxy S27 dummy units that look like the latest leaks, and Samsung fans aren’t having it.

Industry observers note that at this point, it’s anyone’s best guess as to what the Galaxy S27 series looks like, but it’s seeming surer and surer that Samsung will be giving the series a big redesign this coming year. Chris Franklin, a writer at SammyGuru, posted an unboxing video of the Galaxy S27 on X, citing that there’s a possibility the unboxing is AI-created — there are some eyebrow-raising reflections here, but it’s hard to tell for certain. The design looks similar to the “confirmed” renders that leaked a few days ago, although there are some subtle differences.

Sources indicate that I don't think much about the design of phones, they're essentially all the same, especially when considering you're looking at the front 90% of the time, but I've always found the Galaxy's vertical camera layout to be the least attractive of any of the major phones. I think this looks much better.

Sources indicate that unsurprisingly, another leak from earlier in the month has a similar look but, again, with subtle differences. So far, all the major leaks in the past few months are pointing to Samsung outfitting the Galaxy S27 series with a raised camera island that looks extremely similar to Apple’s design on the iPhone 17 Pro and 18 Pro series.

Samsung isn’t alone here. The Xiaomi 18 series and Honor Magic 9 Pro series both have eerily similar designs, and many other 2026 and 2027 phones have followed suit. The most obvious problem with Samsung’s potential design (and, by extension, Apple’s) is the raised camera lenses, which protrude above the raised camera island. Xiaomi’s island is flat, following Google’s idea that a camera bar should protect the lenses and also keep the phone from wobbling or feeling off-balance.

It has been revealed that drama has already taken off on X (formerly Twitter), where Noah Cat reposted the video, and it seems Samsung fans aren’t happy. Samsung has needed to change up the vertical camera bar for years, as it has regularly gotten in the way of Qi2 and MagSafe magnetic accessories. This new design might help that, but it seems fans wanted Samsung to return to the Galaxy S10 horizontal camera bar days, not this new iPhone-esque raised island.
